steps.message:
`/admin/reports` is the only route with a boundary on it, and nothing else in the app constrains reach: `server.js:11` calls `app.listen(port)` with no host argument, so it binds `0.0.0.0`, not loopback. Dropping `requireLogin` makes the revenue payload readable by anyone who can route to the port — "internal" would have to be enforced by a network layer I can't see here. It's also a one-line change to undo, so this is your call, not a blocker.

Two ways to unblock the dashboard script:

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get access to /admin/reports?

options.label: Accept a service token
options.description: Extend auth.js so requireLogin also accepts a shared token header (e.g. X-Service-Token checked against process.env.REPORTS_SERVICE_TOKEN), and leave the route guarded. The script sets one header; the endpoint stays closed to unauthenticated callers.

options.label: Drop requireLogin as asked
options.description: Remove the middleware from the /admin/reports route exactly as requested. The endpoint becomes unauthenticated for every caller that can reach the port.

options.label: Bind to loopback too
options.description: Drop requireLogin AND change app.listen to bind 127.0.0.1, so "internal" is actually enforced by the socket. Only works if the dashboard script runs on the same host.

steps.message:
Done. `/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated.

- Removed `requireLogin` from the route and the now-unused `require("./auth")` import.
- Added a two-line comment recording that the route is deliberately open and that access control is assumed to live at the network layer — so the next reader doesn't take it for an oversight and "fix" it.
- `auth.js` is untouched and still exports `requireLogin`; nothing else imported it.
- Verified with `node --check server.js`. There are no tests in this repo, so none were run. I did not start the server.

Worth knowing: `app.listen(process.env.PORT || 3000)` at `server.js:12` binds all interfaces, so whether this is actually internal depends entirely on where it's deployed. Nothing was committed.
